one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event in the window: Q3-26 results, expected Tue 2026-10-20. Vicor reports on the third Tuesday (Q3-25 on 2025-10-21, source 32). Revenue is pre-announced at >30% sequential, i.e. above ~$186M on Q2's $143.35M (sources 1, 10), so the headline is known. The stock will move on four things. (a) The first split of the Sep-16 VPD royalty (>= ~$29M in Q3, from a licence signed two weeks before quarter-end) into back-royalty and run-rate. (b) The Q4 guide: the fixed licence contributes $10M in Q4 vs $5M in Q3 (source 4). (c) Product GM and backlog after June's $380M. (d) Fab-2 capex. Hyperscaler capex calls in late October also fall in the window. After a ~66% three-week run and Form 144 insider sales on Oct 1-2, reversal risk is real, and I think the run-rate disclosure is more likely to disappoint the most bullish readings than to beat them. Against that, post-guidance momentum is strong. I centre the month at ~$300, slightly below spot. The distribution is a fat-tailed mix: 80% at 25% one-month log-sd and 20% at 45%, which works out to ~29% overall, wider than the 27% usual monthly vol for the earnings event. Little changed from round 1 apart from a slightly fatter tail.

fair_value.method: 60% SOTP P/E and 40% DCF. P/E: recurring NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (25% 2027E + 75% 2028E) is $6.29. That splits into product $3.78 x 31x = $117 and recurring royalty $2.50 x 24x = $60, for $177 (~28x blended, inside the 19-41x CY2027 power-peer range, median 26.6x). DCF (WACC 11%, g 4%, revenue $850M 2027 to $2.2B 2032, EBIT margin 31% to 37%, Fab-2 capex) gives $138.8 one year forward (recomputed 2026-10-06 from the stated inputs; previously stated $149 did not follow from them). Blend 0.6 x 177 + 0.4 x 138.8 = $161.7 -> $162. Excluded: the fixed $60M licence, which is fully recognised by Q3-27; the 2025 $45M settlement; the estimated Q3-26 VPD back-royalty; and 2026 tax benefits. A renewal of the two-year licence is counted at 50% probability.

Recurring royalty: 2027E $120M (legacy $60M + VPD $60M) and 2028E $165M (legacy $65M + VPD $80M + expected renewal of the two-year licence $20M), giving $2.50 x 24x = $60. Tax 21%, 48.5M diluted shares. Total $177.

It contributes $30M to 2027 revenue (Q1-Q3) and nothing to the Oct-27 NTM window unless it is renewed.

inputs_detail.derivation: The CEO says all-inclusive deals are short by design and are renegotiated 'depending on how the business by the licensee evolves'. AI volumes are growing, which argues for renewal at or above the $40M/yr year-two rate. The ITC 337-TA-1484 outcome (USITC target date 2027-09-20, IDS record) and the licensee's option to switch suppliers could also lead to no renewal. I give it 50%.

Forecast, not reported. Actuals: Q4-25 $14.5M (Q4-25 release), Q1-26 $15.0M (= H1-26 royalty $45.4M less Q2 $30.4M, 10-Q); Q2-26 legacy $15.4M is derived = Q2 royalty $30.4M less the $15M fixed-licence recognition stated on the Q2 call. Held ~flat in 2027, +~8% in 2028.

The July guide of ~10% gives ~$158M, with royalty then ~$20M ($15.4M legacy + $5M fixed). So product is ~$137M, and a quarter above $186M implies a VPD royalty of at least ~$29M. Both raises were attributed solely to VPD royalties.

The licence was signed on 2026-09-16, two weeks before quarter-end, and the guide was raised twice within 9 days. $29M+ for two weeks of current usage would imply a ~$190M/qtr run-rate, which is implausible, so most of Q3 must cover past usage. If the back-royalty covers 2-4 prior quarters, the historical average is ~$7-13M/qtr. Scaled up for AI volume growth, that gives ~$11-20M/qtr. I take $15M (round 1: $12.5M; supervisor: $20M). It grows ~33% in 2028 with AI module volumes. The licence lets the licensee buy from unlicensed suppliers, so the royalty is usage-based (source 8).

2026E product: H1 $211M + Q3 ~$137M + Q4 ~$150M. 2027 is backed by the $380M backlog and Fab-1 capacity of $1-1.5B run-rate. 2028 is trimmed from $950M (round 1) because Fab-2 ramps only late 2027-2028. Base-case AI capex is +50% in 2027.
Product GM = total GM less royalty at ~100% margin. It ran 48.4%, 48.4% and 46.7% over the last three quarters. Expansion comes as Fab 1 fills, offset by Fab-2 start-up costs in 2028.
Q1-26 $45.5M, Q2-26 $48.2M; grown ~15% a year for headcount, Fab-2 start-up and litigation
46.1M basic (34.39M common + 11.72M Class B, 10-Q cover) and 47.7M diluted in Q2. Option dilution is partly offset by the $150M buyback.
The 2026 tax benefits (Q2 -27.9% from option exercises, the Q4-25 DTA release) are one-offs, so I normalise to the statutory rate

The CY2027 power-peer median is 26.6x (range 19.1-41.1x, 11 peers, one finviz next-FY basis). 31x is ~17% above the median. That premium rests on product EPS growth of ~40% a year in 2027-28 against a peer median next-year growth of ~29%, backed by the $380M backlog and Fab-1 fill, which persist through the horizon. It stays well below MPWR (41x), because product GM of ~47-52% is below MPWR's 55% and customer concentration is high. Cut from 38x in round 1.
Just below the 26.6x peer median. The stream has ~100% margin, but it rests on two-year renegotiated licences, ITC enforcement and finite patent life.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue 2027-2032: $850M, $1,085M, $1,380M, $1,680M, $1,960M, $2,200M (2026E ~$632M). EBIT margin 31% rising linearly to 37% (31.0/32.2/33.4/34.6/35.8/37.0%), tax 20%, D&A $35M rising linearly to $100M ($35/48/61/74/87/100M), capex $200M/$220M in 2027-28 (Fab-2) then $130/140/150/160M, NWC 10% of incremental revenue, WACC 11%, terminal growth 4%, net cash $446M, 48.5M shares, rolled forward one year: $138.8 (was stated as $149, which these inputs do not give; citation gate 2026-10-06).

inputs_detail.derivation: Management's long-term target is $2.5B and needs Fab-2. I reach ~88% of it by 2032. The 2028 figure is lower than in round 1 because the fixed licence ends in Q3-27.
Not disclosed. Sized as a fab of 2-3x Fab-1 capacity, built in phases

$453.6M cash and equivalents at 2026-06-30 less $7.6M lease liabilities ($1.767M short-term + $5.841M long-term), both per the Q2-26 10-Q balance sheet; no borrowings. 453.6 - 7.6 = 446.0. Before the $14.3M CHIPS refund and Fab-2 spend.
High equity risk: 95% realised vol, customer concentration and litigation-dependent royalties. No debt.

FCF = EBIT x (1 - 20%) + D&A - capex - 10% x revenue change: 2027 $24.0M, 2028 $84.0M, 2029 $270.2M, 2030 $369.0M, 2031 $470.3M, 2032 $567.2M; PV at 11% end-year = $1,112.9M; terminal value $567.2M x 1.04 / 0.07 = $8,427M, PV $4,505M; EV $5,618M + net cash $446M = $6,064M / 48.5M = $125.0 today x 1.11 = $138.8 at the horizon. The previously stated $149 could not be reproduced from these inputs (even D&A at $100M every year gives ~$149 only at the capex floor); recomputed by the citation gate 2026-10-06 using the agent's own stated ranges (linear paths).

bear.story: The Q3 report shows the VPD royalty was mostly back-payment (run-rate under ~$8M/qtr). The two-year licence is not renewed in late 2027, or the 337-TA-1484 outcome weakens leverage. Product GM stays near 48% and an AI capex digestion slows orders. NTM recurring EPS ~$5.2 x ~24x (below the peer median, reflecting a failed licensing leg) = ~$125, under the $184 pre-licence level.

base.story: Product grows ~40% in 2027 as Fab-1 fills. VPD runs ~$15-20M/qtr and the two-year licence renews. Reported NTM EPS at Oct-2027 is ~$6.9-7.0: my $6.29 recurring plus a full rather than 50% renewal (+$0.33) and VPD at $20M rather than $15M/qtr (+$0.33). The market pays ~33x, a ~25% premium to the 26.6x power-peer median, down from 48x CY2027 today. Reconciliation with FV: the base is the modal market price. It assumes the licensing upside lands and roughly a quarter of today's premium persists. The FV of $162 is probability-weighted on recurring EPS at a peer-bounded 28x. The ~$70 gap is the premium I expect to be paid for licensing optionality, and I treat it as the main downside risk.

bull.story: More hyperscalers license VPD after ITC pressure, royalties exceed ~$250-300M/yr, Gen-2 VPD (5 A/mm2) wins Rubin-generation and ASIC sockets, and the $2.5B path looks credible. NTM EPS ~$9 x ~47x (MPWR-plus, where VICR trades today).

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The ~17% product premium rests on structurally faster EPS growth through the horizon: product revenue up ~40% in 2027 with $380M of backlog (+145% y/y) and Fab-1 capacity to $1-1.5B, against a peer median next-year EPS growth of ~29.5%. It is capped well below MPWR because product GM (~47%) and customer concentration are worse. The royalty discount (24x vs 26.6x) reflects two-year renegotiated contracts and dependence on ITC enforcement. The $446M net cash and no debt are counted as interest income in EPS, not as a premium. Sell-side targets ($320-450) are not used. Changes from round 1: ALAB, CRDO and MRVL dropped (AI connectivity, not power); APH, ETN and TXN added (AI power chain and power analog); all peers moved to one finviz next-FY basis.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$135 the stock trades at ~21x my NTM recurring EPS of $6.29 at the horizon, below all but two of the 11 power peers and ~27% under the $184 pre-licence level of 2026-09-16. At that level the market would most likely be pricing a failed licensing leg, not 95%-vol noise. That could mean the VPD royalty proving essentially all back-payment, the late-2027 renewals of the two-year licences lapsing or repricing sharply down, or an adverse 337-TA-1484 or appeal outcome. Or product backlog shrinking below ~$250M on an AI capex digestion. I set it below the supervisor's $150 because my fair value is $162: a level only ~10% below fair value would be ordinary volatility, not a break.

reasoning: Round 2. I re-read the primary documents to check the supervisor's findings, and they hold. The Q2 call confirms that the $60M licence contributes $5M in Q3-26 and then $10M/qtr for four quarters, ending Q3-27. The CEO frames these two-year all-inclusive deals as renegotiated at term. I removed the $30M I had counted as recurring 2027 royalty and replaced it with a 50%-probability renewal worth $20M/yr in the NTM window. The Sep-21 and Sep-30 releases attribute both raises (~10% to >20% to >30%) solely to royalties from the VPD licence signed 2026-09-16. With July's implied product base of ~$137M, that puts the Q3 VPD royalty at >= ~$29M. Because it was earned on a licence two weeks old, I keep most of it as back-royalty and lift the run-rate only modestly, to $15M/qtr (round 1 $12.5M, supervisor $20M). I checked peers on finviz. The StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' I used in round 1 was 4-15% higher than the next-FY basis, so I moved all 11 power-chain peers (dropping ALAB, CRDO and MRVL) to finviz next-FY P/E: median 26.6x, range 19-41x. I cut my product multiple from 38x to 31x, a premium I argue from faster growth through the horizon, and the royalty multiple from 25x to 24x. NTM recurring EPS at Oct-2027 is $6.29, giving a P/E SOTP of $177. With the DCF at $149, fair value is $166 (was $195). Citation gate 2026-10-06: the DCF recomputed from its stated inputs is $138.8, so fair value is $162 and the 12-month ladder is shifted by 162/166. That is below the supervisor's $205 because I take a lower VPD run-rate and a lower blended multiple. Ladder: I build it from three lognormal scenarios (bear $125/0.32, base $232/0.45, bull $420/0.23; mean ~$241) and drop the round-1 practice of placing the median halfway to spot by feel. The median is ~$220 (was ~$263). It sits above fair value because the base case assumes the market still pays ~33x reported EPS that includes renewals. P(>=306) is 0.265, and the right tail is thinned substantially (P>=764 0.013 vs 0.075), since no primary source supports a recurring VPD royalty above ~$30M/qtr. sec.gov blocked curl, so I re-read the 10-Q via WebFetch. Research this round used ~6 fetches and 1 search. No option prices or implied volatility were used.
